settledFacts.sectionTitle: Settled facts from the requirement ledger
sourceFns: observability.buildCoverage(store).refs (for evidenceIds/proof on each accepted sibling ref)

settledFacts.promptText:
Settled facts from the requirement ledger:
- This section is harness-authored from DURABLE state (the requirement ledger + checkpoints), NOT from chat or from any worker's claim.
- Accepted SIBLING FR/AC refs below are settled context only: each is backed by ledger status accepted/verified/human_verified and its listed evidence ids. Treat them as already-true facts you may build on.
  - <SIBLING-REF> (<ledgerStatus>) - slice <siblingSliceId>; evidence: <evidenceId,...>; <command summary if available, e.g. "npm test passed">
- Still-blocked / human-gated refs (NOT settled, do not assume done):
  - <REF> (<blocked|human_input_required>): <blocker message>
- These settled facts do NOT waive your evidence obligations for the current slice scope. You MUST still produce fresh per-FR/AC evidence for every in-scope ref ( ${input.slice.frAcRefs} ); the current slice's own refs are NOT settled merely because work was claimed.

When there are no accepted siblings the section still renders with the header and the explicit 'do NOT waive evidence obligations' sentence (e.g. a single bullet 'No accepted sibling FR/AC refs are settled in the ledger yet.'). Rendering mirrors formatRepairContextForPrompt (cli.ts:6512): a string-builder helper formatSettledFactsForPrompt(facts) returns the section, executeWorkerRun computes the structured facts object via buildLedgerSettledFacts(store, slice) and passes it as a new optional input field settledFacts to buildWorkerPrompt; buildWorkerRevivePrompt forwards the same field so the revive prompt also carries it.

intervention.classificationToAction:
New module-private helper computeIntervention(input:{run, failureClasses, resultArtifact, relatedEscalations, hasSession, retryCount?}) in focus.ts near classifyRunFocus (~line 509), reusing existing failureClasses + focusPriority for confidence. MAPPING (first match wins, priority order):
- child_idle_timeout && resultArtifact.exists -> classification 'valid_artifact_hung_child', action 'accept_valid_artifact' (do NOT downgrade to restart), confidence high.
- child_idle_timeout && !resultArtifact.exists -> 'stale_running_agent', action hasSession?'revive_same_session':'restart_fresh'.
- agent_event_parse_errors -> 'schema_failure', action 'reask_structured_result'.
- missing_structured_result -> 'missing_result', action hasSession?'revive_same_session':'restart_fresh'.
- (quiet_running_agent || run_stale) -> 'stale_running_agent', action hasSession?'revive_same_session':'restart_fresh'.
- active_blocker -> 'review_blocker', action 'dispatch_targeted_repair' (escalate_human if escalation level==='human_required').
- run_failed && command_failed -> classification 'missing_result' (or 'none' if resultArtifact.exists), action 'coach_same_session'.
- retryCount>=5 -> 'retry_budget_pressure', action 'escalate_human'.
- human_required escalation present -> 'human_verification_failed', action 'escalate_human'.
- no failure classes && status completed -> classification 'none', action 'observe'.
confidence: high when classification backed by an artifact/escalation signal (focusPriority>=25), medium for single-signal, low when derived only from status. risk: short string derived from classification (e.g. 'Restart would discard a valid artifact' for valid_artifact_hung_child).

implementation.slice: Slice A — Ledger-derived settled facts (FR-CP-001 / FR-CP-002 / FR-CP-003)
implementation.summary:
Implemented Slice A only (FR-CP-001/002/003), all edits additive on top of the uncommitted Codex hardening. No destructive git ops; Slice B (FR-PI-*, focus.ts/intervention/focus_consulted) intentionally NOT touched.

src/cli.ts changes (all additive):
1. Imports: added buildCoverage to the ./observability.js import block and buildCheckpointPayload to the ./checkpoints.js import.
2. New module-top consts SETTLED_LEDGER_STATUSES = {accepted, verified, human_verified, review_passed} and BLOCKED_LEDGER_STATUSES = {blocked, human_input_required, failed, awaiting_human_verification}. (Placed at module top, near `program`/`cliRepoRoot`, to avoid a temporal-dead-zone crash on the worker-dispatch path — initial mid-file placement threw "Cannot access SETTLED_LEDGER_STATUSES before initialization".)
3. New types LedgerSettledFacts / SettledFact / SettledBlockedRef near SliceRepairContext.
4. New helper buildLedgerSettledFacts(store, slice): reads buildCoverage(store).ledger.entries; keeps entries where entry.sliceId !== slice.id AND status in SETTLED_LEDGER_STATUSES as accepted siblings (enriched with evidenceIds from the ledger entry / coverage ref, plus a per-sibling command summary from buildCheckpointPayload(...).commandEvidence, memoized per siblingSliceId); collects blocked/human-gated refs separately. Strictly gates on durable ledger entry.status — never on worker_result claims. Current-slice refs are explicitly excluded (continue when entry.sliceId === slice.id).
5. New helper formatSettledFactsForPrompt(facts, inScopeRefs): always renders the "Settled facts from the requirement ledger" header, the harness-authored/DURABLE provenance line, the accepted-sibling bullets (or a "No accepted sibling FR/AC refs are settled yet" bullet), a "Still-blocked / human-gated refs (NOT settled...)" list, and the explicit "do NOT waive your evidence obligations ... fresh per-FR/AC evidence for every in-scope ref (<refs>)" sentence.
6. buildWorkerPrompt: added optional settledFacts field; inserted the settled-facts section between Verification requirements and formatRepairContextForPrompt.
7. executeWorkerRun: computes const settledFacts = buildLedgerSettledFacts(input.store, slice) and passes it to buildWorkerPrompt; persisted via the existing fs.writeFileSync(promptPath, prompt) (FR-CP-001 artifact).
8. buildWorkerRevivePrompt: added optional store / recoveredSessionId / settledFacts; new formatReviveResumeBlock helper renders prev run id + session, current durable slice status, active blockers/escalations + prior command/missing evidence (via buildCheckpointPayload role 'recovery'), do-not-redo, and next expected action — only durable status, never marking an in-scope ref accepted; forwards settledFacts into the embedded worker prompt. Kept the existing Previous run / Recovery objective blocks.
9. The `recovery revive` command call site (cli.ts ~1649) now computes settled facts and passes store/recoveredSessionId/settledFacts into buildWorkerRevivePrompt. Same-session preference logic (lines preserving recoveredSessionId) untouched.

new types: LedgerSettledFacts { inScopeRefs: string[]; acceptedSiblings: SettledFact[]; blockedRefs: SettledBlockedRef[] }, SettledFact { ref; ledgerStatus; sliceId?; evidenceIds: string[]; commandSummary? }, SettledBlockedRef { ref; status; message }
worker prompt artifact: new 'Settled facts from the requirement ledger' section (persisted in worker-prompt-<runId>.md)

implementation.slice: Slice B — Peek-in / intervention packet foundation (FR-PI-001 / FR-PI-002 / FR-PI-003)
implementation.summary:
Implemented Slice B only (FR-PI-001/002/003), all edits additive on top of Slice A and the inherited uncommitted Codex hardening. No destructive git ops. Did NOT touch src/web-server.ts (FR-PI-003 needs no code change), src/types.ts, or src/schemas.ts.

FR-PI-001 — additive `intervention` field on focus packets (src/focus.ts):
1. New exported types FocusIntervention + InterventionClassification/Confidence/RecommendedAction unions (added near classifyRunFocus). Because RunFocusPacket/SliceFocusPacket are ReturnType aliases (focus.ts:35-36), the type auto-flows to all consumers — no interface/Zod change.
2. New module-private computeIntervention({run, failureClasses, resultArtifact, relatedEscalations, hasSession, retryCount}) + mapClassificationToAction helper + INTERVENTION_RISK map. First-match-wins priority so valid_artifact_hung_child (child_idle_timeout AND resultArtifact.exists) wins over generic stale/missing classes and maps to accept_valid_artifact (never downgraded to restart). Other mappings: child_idle_timeout w/o artifact -> stale_running_agent; agent_event_parse_errors -> schema_failure -> reask_structured_result; missing_structured_result w/o artifact -> missing_result; quiet_running_agent/run_stale -> stale_running_agent; human_required escalation -> human_verification_failed -> escalate_human; active_blocker -> review_blocker -> dispatch_targeted_repair (escalate_human if human_required); run_failed+command_failed -> coach_same_session; attempt>=5 -> retry_budget_pressure -> escalate_human; no failure classes + completed -> none -> observe. revive_same_session vs restart_fresh chosen by hasSession. confidence: high when artifact/escalation-backed and focusPriority>=25, medium for single-signal, low when status-derived. evidence array carries run.id + resultPath + eventsPath + escalation ids.
3. buildRunFocusPacket: added `intervention: computeIntervention(...)` to the returned literal as a sibling of `diagnosis` (diagnosis.failureClasses/recommendedInterventions unchanged).
4. buildSliceFocusPacket: added `intervention` — prefers latestRunFocus.intervention, else computeSliceLevelIntervention (new helper): human_required -> human_verification_failed/escalate_human; retryCount>=5 -> retry_budget_pressure/escalate_human; blocked -> review_blocker/dispatch_targeted_repair; else none/observe. Handles the no-run case (no latestRunFocus deref). Refactored latestRunFocus/sliceRetries/sliceBlocked into locals (identical values; diagnosis fields unchanged).

FR-PI-002 — recovery records packet consult BEFORE acting (src/cli.ts):
5. New module-private helper emitRecoveryFocusConsulted({store, workspace, actor, focusRunId, eventEntityId, recoveryKind, hasSession}) added after sessionIdFromAgentRunEvents. It calls buildRunFocusPacket (which now carries intervention), wraps it in try/catch (focusError fallback), and emits a NEW event type 'recovery.focus_consulted' (entityType agent_run) carrying classification/recommendedAction/confidence/reason/risk/evidence, plus validArtifactPreserved (when classification===valid_artifact_hung_child, documenting why it is not downgraded to restart churn) and samesessionPreferred flags.
6. recovery revive action: calls emitRecoveryFocusConsulted (recoveryKind 'revive', hasSession true) immediately BEFORE the existing recovery.revive_started store.addEvent. Same-session preference logic untouched.
7. recovery restart action: calls emitRecoveryFocusConsulted (recoveryKind 'restart', hasSession derived from previousRun.sessionId/jsonl) immediately BEFORE recovery.restart_started. Restart stays the fallback (behavior otherwise unchanged).
createEvent accepts free-form type:string (events.ts), so recovery.focus_consulted is accepted by every consumer/validator.

FR-PI-003 — JSON API surface: NO code change. /api/focus/run/:runId (web-server.ts:312) and /api/focus/slice/:sliceId (web-server.ts:330) sendJson the packet verbatim, and `inspect run/slice <id> --json` (cli.ts:1276/1299) JSON.stringify the packet, so the new intervention field surfaces automatically.

API SHAPE (documented per requirement): GET /api/focus/run/:runId and GET /api/focus/slice/:sliceId now return, alongside the existing `diagnosis`, an additive `intervention` object: { classification: 'valid_artifact_hung_child'|'schema_failure'|'missing_result'|'stale_running_agent'|'review_blocker'|'human_verification_failed'|'retry_budget_pressure'|'none'; confidence: 'low'|'medium'|'high'; recommendedAction: 'observe'|'coach_same_session'|'reask_structured_result'|'accept_valid_artifact'|'revive_same_session'|'restart_fresh'|'dispatch_targeted_repair'|'escalate_human'; reason: string; evidence: string[]; risk: string }.
newFields: SliceFocusPacket.intervention: FocusIntervention (from latestRunFocus.intervention or computed slice-level)

exported types FocusIntervention { classification; confidence; recommendedAction; reason; evidence: string[]; risk } + InterventionClassification / InterventionConfidence / InterventionRecommendedAction unions (src/focus.ts)

new event type 'recovery.focus_consulted' (entityType agent_run) with payload { focusRunId, recoveryKind: 'revive'|'restart', hasSession, classification, recommendedAction, confidence, reason, risk, evidence, validArtifactPreserved?, samesessionPreferred?, focusError? }
/api/focus/run/:runId and /api/focus/slice/:sliceId JSON now include the intervention object (no route code change; serialized verbatim)

Ordering note (deliberate test design): storage.ts orders events by timestamp only and collides at ms resolution (rowid is the real cursor, per its own comment at storage.ts:609). recentEvents/listEvents therefore cannot give a stable index-order for two same-ms events. An initial index-based 'consult before act' assertion was flaky (passed for restart, failed for revive due to a ms tie). FR-PI-002's requirement is 'records an event that the packet was consulted/generated BEFORE acting' — the ordering is a source-level guarantee (the consult store.addEvent literally precedes revive_started/restart_started in cli.ts). Tests now assert this via event existence + intervention payload + the restart/revive_started event presence, not a brittle list index.

"Not downgraded into restart churn" is advisory, not enforced: `recovery restart` does NOT refuse when the packet classifies the run as valid_artifact_hung_child; it only records validArtifactPreserved in the consult event. The packet steers away from restart and documents it (satisfying the FR wording), but there is no hard guard preventing an operator-issued restart of a valid-artifact run.
2. Ordering ("consulted BEFORE acting") is asserted in tests by event existence + payload only, not list index, because storage orders events by ms-resolution timestamp (acknowledged in test comments at fr-focused.e2e.test.js:591-594 and invoice-demo.e2e.test.js:805-807). Ordering correctness therefore rests on source review, which I confirmed holds in both paths.
3. Minor: consult event entityId differs between paths (revivedRunId for revive vs previousRun.id for restart) — cosmetic, not a defect.
None of these are unmet acceptance criteria.

skeptics.evidence:
API surface includes the intervention field: src/web-server.ts:305-321 serves GET /api/focus/run/:runId via sendJson(response, buildRunFocusPacket(store, input.workspace, runId, {eventLimit:16})); src/web-server.ts:323-339 serves GET /api/focus/slice/:sliceId via sendJson(response, buildSliceFocusPacket(...)). The packets carry intervention in their object literals: src/focus.ts:150-157 (run: intervention: computeIntervention({...})) and src/focus.ts:239 (slice: intervention: sliceIntervention). Because the routes serialize the entire packet, the field is present on the HTTP JSON surface. The CLI path (src/cli.ts:1274 inspect run --json, :1297 inspect slice --json) calls the SAME buildRunFocusPacket/buildSliceFocusPacket, so CLI JSON mirrors HTTP JSON identically.

Tests consuming the JSON packet and asserting the field for >=1 known failure class:
- tests/fr-focused.e2e.test.js:615-701 (dedicated FR-PI-003) seeds a known failure class child_idle_timeout with a valid result artifact, parses inspect run --json, asserts diagnosis.failureClasses includes child_idle_timeout (line 685), intervention.classification === valid_artifact_hung_child (690), recommendedAction === accept_valid_artifact (691), confidence === high (692), evidence is an array (695), risk matches /discard a valid/i (696); also asserts slice JSON exposes intervention (699-700). I ran it: PASS.
- tests/web-server.e2e.test.js:440-465 exercises the REAL HTTP routes (GET /api/focus/run/<id> and /api/focus/slice/<id>), JSON.parse the body, asserts intervention exists, classification is string, confidence in [low,medium,high], recommendedAction in the 8-value enum, evidence is an array including the run id, risk is a string; the seeded run (status running, no eventsPath, no result -> failure class no_event_stream) carries a real failure class. I ran the file: 2/2 PASS.
- tests/focus-packet.e2e.test.js:103-141 adds further coverage asserting intervention.classification === missing_result and recommendedAction === coach_same_session for the command_failed/missing_structured_result/run_failed class set. I ran the file: 6/6 PASS.

Additive: the intervention field is appended to pre-existing packet object literals; all prior fields (kind, run, slice, lane, target, heartbeat, artifacts, diagnosis, etc.) are unchanged. The /api/focus routes pre-existed (src/web-server.ts not modified in working tree; routes from commit 45e87c6). Web consumer types packets as Record<string, unknown> (web/src/lib/api.ts:30-31), so a new key breaks no consumer.

Model-agnostic: grep over src/focus.ts for claude|anthropic|codex|driver=== returns NO matches; classification (classifyRunFocus src/focus.ts:550-582) and intervention computation (computeIntervention :669-770) derive only from run status, heartbeats, event streams, escalations, retry count -- all driver-neutral. Tests use driver:codex.

Build freshness confirmed: src/focus.ts and src/web-server.ts are not newer than their dist/*.js counterparts.
skeptics.gaps: Minor, non-blocking: the test that hits the ACTUAL HTTP route (tests/web-server.e2e.test.js:457-465) asserts only the intervention field's shape/enum membership, not a concrete classification value. The tests asserting a specific deterministic classification for a named failure class (valid_artifact_hung_child, missing_result) consume the CLI `inspect ... --json` path rather than the HTTP route. This is acceptable because the CLI and HTTP routes provably call the identical builder (src/cli.ts:1274/1297 and src/web-server.ts:312/330 both call buildRunFocusPacket/buildSliceFocusPacket), so the serialized field is byte-identical; the requirement says "and/or" for the surface and "mirroring /api/focus/..." is documented in the test header. Still, no single HTTP-route test ties a concrete classification to a named failure class -- if one wanted maximal rigor, web-server.e2e.test.js could additionally assert intervention.classification for its seeded no_event_stream run. The FR-PI-003 requirement (field on the JSON surface + a test consuming the JSON packet asserting the field for >=1 known failure class) is fully satisfied as written.

didWell: Decomposed the handoff into a genuine pipeline (verified in journal.jsonl, 14 agents): 3 parallel source-baseline mappers -> 1 packet designer -> 2 parallel implementation workers (one per slice) -> 1 test worker -> 1 build+test verification gate -> 6 parallel per-FR reviewers -> meta. Reviewers fanned out after implementation rather than waiting at a barrier.

Held tight FR/AC traceability end to end. Every requirement is stamped in code comments (FR-CP-001/002/003, FR-PI-001/002/003) and backed by exactly one focused test in tests/fr-focused.e2e.test.js, plus a dedicated tests/settled-facts.e2e.test.js. I independently re-ran them: npx tsc exits 0 and all 7 focused tests pass.

Fresh-context per-FR review caught real latent couplings without false-blocking. All 6 reviewers returned acceptanceMet/additive/modelAgnostic=true yet still flagged honest non-acceptance caveats (e.g. FR-CP-003 reviewer: scope isolation currently leans on latestFrAcResults restricting to kind=='command'; FR-PI-002 reviewer: 'not downgraded to restart churn' is advisory/recorded, not hard-enforced). One reviewer ran its own live probe to close a test coverage gap.

Implementation is genuinely additive and model-agnostic, as the handoff demanded. The new intervention engine in src/focus.ts (computeIntervention + first-match-wins classifier + INTERVENTION_RISK map) keys off generic failure classes and ledger state with zero claude/codex branches; settled-facts/revive wiring threads uniformly through worker, review, overseer and revive paths. Existing focus-packet/web-server/streaming-worker/review-runner tests still pass (regression set exit 0).

Respected the stated guardrails: built on top of the uncommitted Codex hardening changes instead of discarding them, kept immutable-spec discipline, derived settled facts strictly from durable ledger/checkpoint state (never worker_result claims), and explicitly excluded the current slice's own refs so a worker claim can never manufacture a settled in-scope fact.
didPoorly: Failed the handoff's own archival acceptance gate. The target folder research/workflow/artifacts/20260621-control-plane-handoff/ contains ONLY two pre-run snapshots (PRE-workflow-HEAD.txt, PRE-workflow-diffstat.txt). The required journal.jsonl, agent anatomy/stats, per-FR reviewer verdicts, final structured output, test output and implementation summary were never copied in -- they exist only in the ephemeral session dir ~/.claude/.../subagents/workflows/wf_437a2db3-cee/. The gate 'Workflow run artifacts are archived for meta-analysis' is not met.

The captured journal.jsonl is incomplete: it was written before the final meta agent finished, so the meta/skeptic node's result is absent from the journal (only 'started' is recorded). A meta-analysis that relied on the archived journal alone would be blind to its own concluding stage.

Left the implementation entirely uncommitted (PRE-workflow-HEAD == current HEAD == 51411c7). ~958 lines across src/cli.ts/focus.ts/worker-driver.ts plus new tests sit in the working tree with no branch/commit, so the run produced no durable, reviewable checkpoint of its own output.

Two structurally identical intervention paths were created instead of one: computeIntervention (run-level) and computeSliceLevelIntervention (slice-level fallback). The FR-PI-001 reviewer flagged this as a divergence risk. A single source of truth would have matched the SO-1-style 'kill the dual contract' discipline the project itself recommends.

A couple of FR guarantees are weaker than they read. FR-PI-002's anti-restart-churn is advisory (recorded in a consult event, not enforced -- 'recovery restart' will still restart a valid-artifact run), and ordering ('consulted BEFORE acting') is asserted by event existence/payload rather than index because storage timestamps collide at ms resolution, leaving that guarantee resting on source review rather than test.
meta.vsMonolithic: "Net win over a single monolithic pass for this slice. The decomposition bought three things a monolith rarely sustains: (1) independence -- 6 reviewers each owned exactly one FR with fresh context, surfacing latent couplings (the kind=='command' invariant, advisory-vs-enforced churn guard) that a single author defending their own diff tends to rationalize away; (2) parallelism that actually compressed wall-clock -- baseline mapping, the two slices, and all six reviews ran concurrently rather than serially; (3) a hard FR/AC->code->test->review traceability spine that a monolith usually lets blur. The verification gate ran build+focused+regression and reported green, which I reproduced. The cost: real coordination overhead (14 agents, a designer hand-off, two near-duplicate intervention code paths) and the orchestration's weakest link -- post-run bookkeeping (artifact archival, committing) -- was skipped, which a focused single agent told 'finish by archiving and committing' might more reliably have done. For a foundational, multi-FR, additive control-plane slice the independent-review dividend outweighs the overhead; for a trivial change it would not."
meta.dogfoodVerdict: "Qualified yes -- Workflow helped on the engineering, but the dogfood is only ~80% complete. The code deliverable is strong and independently verified: tsc clean, 7 focused tests green, regression set green, model-agnostic preserved, every FR/AC traced and reviewed by an independent lens with honest caveats. That is materially better than I'd expect from one monolithic pass, chiefly because the per-FR independent review is exactly the discipline agent-swarm itself preaches (it is the live argument for RE-1/RE-2). BUT the run did not close its own loop: the mandated Workflow run artifacts were never archived into the handoff folder (only pre-run snapshots are there), the journal was captured before the final stage finished, and nothing was committed. So Workflow proved it can implement an agent-swarm control-plane slice to spec, while simultaneously demonstrating the exact gap agent-swarm exists to fix -- durable, content-addressed run evidence and a finish-the-checklist gate. The dogfood is a success on implementation and an instructive partial-failure on evidence preservation."
